name: useUWB
summary: Ultra-wideband radio state and real ranging sessions against a peer device.
plain: Reports whether this phone has the short-range precision radio used for precision spatial tracking and car keys, and ranges against a second UWB device whose address and channel you supply.
description: Chip presence (android.hardware.uwb feature), the enabled state (UwbManager.isUwbEnabled() by reflection, null when apps cannot read it) and ranging service readiness (whether the Android 16 RangingManager service exists) are queried through the native module, carrying source hardware. startRanging(config) opens a real android.ranging.RangingSession (Android 16, API 36+, RAW UWB session) with the peer described by the config: its address, the session id, and optionally the channel, preamble index and key info, all agreed with the peer out of band (BLE, NFC, QR). The call resolves true only when the platform reports the session open; otherwise it resolves false and sessionError carries a status such as needs_peer_configuration, uwb_unsupported, ranging_api_unavailable, uwb_disabled, permission_denied (android.permission.RANGING must be declared and granted by the app), session_active, invalid_parameters or open_failed. measurements holds the latest android.ranging.RangingData sample per peer (distance in meters, azimuth and elevation in degrees, each with the platform's confidence level) and stays empty until the peer answers.

returns.name: isSupported
returns.desc: Whether the UWB chip exists on this device.

returns.name: isEnabled
returns.desc: Whether the radio is switched on in system settings; null when Android does not let apps read it.

returns.name: rangingApiSupported
returns.desc: Whether the Android 16 android.ranging.RangingManager service exists.

returns.name: isRanging
returns.desc: Whether the platform holds an open ranging session. Follows the platform's session events, not the last call.

returns.name: measurements
returns.desc: Latest platform sample per peer device: `deviceId`, `distanceMeters`, `azimuthDegrees`, `elevationDegrees` (null when the platform omitted them), a `*Confidence` of 'low', 'medium' or 'high' for each, `rssi` and `timestampMs`. Empty until the peer answers.

returns.name: sessionInfo
returns.desc: Result of the last start request: `status`, `error`, `sessionId`, `serviceName`, `serviceAvailable`, `rangingFeature`, `timestampMs`.

returns.name: sessionError
returns.desc: Status code and reason when the last start or stop did not succeed, for example `needs_peer_configuration: peerAddress must be hex address bytes`.

returns.name: source
returns.desc: Where the numbers came from. There is no 'simulated' value: a reading is real, derived from real readings, or unavailable.

returns.name: error
returns.desc: Latest failure message, or `null`. Failures are also logged and counted.

actions.name: startRanging(config)
actions.desc: Opens a real UWB ranging session with the peer described by config.

inputs.name: config
inputs.desc: `{ sessionId: number, role: 'initiator' | 'responder', localAddress: string, peerAddress: string, configId?: number (1..6, default 1), channel?: number, preambleIndex?: number, sessionKeyInfo?: string, updateRate?: 'normal' | 'infrequent' | 'frequent', slotDurationMs?: 1 | 2, angleOfArrival?: boolean }`. Addresses and keys are hex bytes (2-byte short or 8-byte extended addresses); channel and preambleIndex go together. All values must match what the peer was given.

actions.output: Resolves true when the platform reported the session open; false with the status and reason in sessionError when the peer configuration is missing or invalid, the device or OS cannot range, a permission is missing, or the platform refused to open. sessionInfo is updated either way.

actions.name: stopRanging()
actions.desc: Closes the running UWB ranging session.
actions.output: Returns `{ wasActive, closed, sessionId, error, timestampMs }`: wasActive is false when nothing was running, and error carries a failure from the platform's stop or close. Returns null when the native module is absent.

agentNote: UWB ranging needs a peer. Never invent addresses, session ids or channels: they come from the device you are ranging with. Without a peer configuration startRanging resolves false with needs_peer_configuration. The ranging API is android.ranging (Android 16+) and requires android.permission.RANGING, which the app must declare in its manifest and request at runtime; without it the status is permission_denied. Report an empty measurements list as 'no peer answered', not as zero distance.
